record.notes: First introduced in 2021 and updated in 2023, according to the Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry (30 Oct 2025). Current text is version 2.0 (December 2025), which updated Sections 1 to 5 and Appendices A to D and removed Appendix E. Earlier versions: 1.1 (June 2023), 1.2 (July 2023), 1.3 (August 2023) and 1.4 (July 2024, which replaced 'Office of the Government Chief Information Officer' with 'Digital Policy Office'). The framework was first developed for government bureaux and departments; this version is adapted for general reference by other organisations. Where the Chinese and English versions differ, the English version prevails.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored and read: the Digital Policy Office's page 'AI and Data Ethics' (digitalpolicy.gov.hk, copy of 11 Oct 2026, re-checked unchanged on 18 Oct 2026), which presents the Ethical AI Framework and links its PDF; the framework PDF, version 2.0 dated December 2025 (copy of 11 Oct 2026, unchanged on 18 Oct 2026), with its amendment history, the 12 Ethical AI Principles, the three lines of defence and the AI Application Impact Assessment reviewed at four stages; and a speech by the Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry of 30 Oct 2025 on the bureau's site (itib.gov.hk, 18 Oct 2026), which says the framework was 'first introduced in 2021' and updated in 2023. date_published is set to the year 2021 from that speech, the only stored source that dates the first version; neither the PDF nor the DPO page dates version 1.0, and the amendment history begins with version 1.1 in June 2023. The PDF and page confirm the title, the issuer, the version and its date, the earlier versions and the content of the summary.

judgment.status_reasoning: The DPO page (re-checked unchanged on 18 Oct 2026; 'Last Revision Date: 30/06/2026') presents the framework and links version 2.0 of December 2025, the latest entry of the amendment history. The framework is guidance with principles, practices and an assessment template for government projects, offered for general reference to other organisations; it is not legislation. Nothing stored shows a later version or withdrawal. 'Published (non-binding, current)' and 'Non-binding' stand.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published '2021' rests on the Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry's speech on the bureau's site ('first introduced in 2021'); it gives only the year, so only the year is recorded (rule 7b). The PDF says the framework was originally developed for government bureaux and departments but does not date that first version; its amendment history begins with version 1.1 in June 2023. date_last_updated 2025-12 is version 2.0's date, which the PDF gives only as 'December 2025'.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A government ethical AI framework with principles, governance and an impact assessment for AI projects; in scope with no note. It began as guidance for government bureaux, but this version is published for general reference, so it is not an internal circular.
judgment.summary_reasoning: The summary was checked against version 2.0 (twelve principles, two of them performance principles; IT Board or CIO as third line for high-risk applications; impact assessment reviewed at four stages) and is kept.
